subject.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite

question: Should PortGuardian’s one-way JSON-to-SQLite migration be an intentional native-runtime exception to the repository’s normal Doctor-owned persistent-state migration rule after the stacked prerequisite lands?
rationale: This is an upgrade and ownership-policy choice with downgrade and mixed-version consequences; tests can validate mechanics but cannot choose the supported migration contract.

options.title: Require Doctor ownership
options.body: Move legacy JSON import, verification, and retirement into an explicit Doctor migration, leaving PortGuardian runtime SQLite-only.

options.title: Approve the native exception
options.body: Accept runtime reconciliation as an intentional macOS-only exception, document the upgrade and downgrade contract, and require live signed-app proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Require Doctor ownership
recommendation.body: Move legacy JSON import, verification, and retirement into an explicit Doctor migration, leaving PortGuardian runtime SQLite-only.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the stacked native-state bootstrap and the proposed PortGuardian storage boundary in the supplied branch history.
